cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Which view explains why a generally aggressive person may act submissively before her/his top boss?
cards.back:
Situationism
A person, who is generally aggressive, may behave in a submissive manner in the presence of her/his top boss.
cards.quote: A person, who is generally aggressive, may behave in a submissive manner in the presence of her/his top boss.
reasons: review:Illustrative case-story; situationism definition card already carries the mark-bearing content

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Name the intelligence correlations reported for twins and siblings.
cards.back:
identical twins reared in different environments correlate 0.72
fraternal twins reared together correlate almost 0.60
brothers and sisters reared together correlate about 0.50
siblings reared apart correlate about 0.25
cards.quote: The intelligence of identical twins reared in different environments correlate 0.72, those of fraternal twins reared together correlate almost 0.60, and those of brothers and sisters reared together correlate about 0.50, while siblings reared apart correlate about 0.25.

source.section: Intelligence: Interplay of Nature and Nurture

reasons: review:Back omits the first reported correlation (identical twins reared together, almost 0.90) though front asks for the correlations; incomplete list, exact back is partial

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Formula: IQ.
cards.back: IQ refers to mental age divided by chronological age, and multiplied by 100.
cards.quote: IQ refers to mental age divided by chronological age, and multiplied by 100.
reasons: review:Formula card does not show the formula NCERT prints (IQ = MA/CA x 100); back is the prose sentence already on the def-iq-stern card (duplicate content)

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: The highly talented are sometimes called "____".
cards.back: The highly talented are sometimes called "prodigies".
cards.quote: The highly talented are sometimes called "prodigies".

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Which Indian test is quite popular among those listed in Table 1.2?
cards.back: Among these, Bhatia's Battery of Performance Tests is quite popular.
cards.quote: Among these, Bhatia's Battery of Performance Tests is quite popular.
reasons: review:Front depends on Table 1.2 (not shown) and several Indian tests exist, so answer not derivable from front; Indian test names are low-yield trivia

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Name the psychologists who have developed creativity tests.
cards.back:
Guilford
Torrance
Khatena
Wallach and Kogan
Paramesh
Baqer Mehdi
Passi
cards.quote: Some of the famous psychologists who have developed creativity tests are Guilford, Torrance, Khatena, Wallach and Kogan, Paramesh, Baqer Mehdi, and Passi.
reasons: review:Seven-name list of test developers is trivia, unrealistic to recall; low exam yield

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Which qualities do Birhor child socialisation practices aim at?
cards.back: Their child socialisation practices are also aimed at making children independent (do many things without help from elders), autonomous (take several decisions for themselves), and achievement-oriented (accept risks and challenges such as those involved in hunting) from an early age of life.
cards.quote: Their child socialisation practices are also aimed at making children independent (do many things without help from elders), autonomous (take several decisions for themselves), and achievement-oriented (accept risks and challenges such as those involved in hunting) from an early age of life.
reasons: review:Birhor case-story filler; the concept is covered by the agricultural vs hunting-gathering card

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Who developed the Sixteen Personality Factor Questionnaire (16 PF), and how did he identify the basic personality structure?
cards.back: This test was developed by Cattell. On the basis of his studies, he identified a large set of personality descriptors, which were subjected to factor analysis to identify the basic personality structure.
cards.quote: This test was developed by Cattell. On the basis of his studies, he identified a large set of personality descriptors, which were subjected to factor analysis to identify the basic personality structure.
reasons: review:Redundant with fact-cattell-16pf and fact-cattell-factor-analysis; same Cattell/factor-analysis fact

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Draw-a-Person Test: name the examples of interpretations given.
cards.back:
Omission of facial features suggests that the person tries to evade a highly conflict-ridden interpersonal relationship.
Graphic emphasis on the neck suggests lack of control over impulses.
Disproportionately large head suggests organic brain disease and preoccupation with headaches.
cards.quote: (1) Omission of facial features suggests that the person tries to evade a highly conflict-ridden interpersonal relationship. (2) Graphic emphasis on the neck suggests lack of control over impulses. (3) Disproportionately large head suggests organic brain disease and preoccupation with headaches.
reasons: review:Illustrative interpretation examples (neck, head, facial features) are case filler, not exam-tested

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: In "Kinds of Self", NCERT distinguishes the "personal" self from which other self?
cards.back: A distinction is made between “personal” and “social” self.
cards.quote: A distinction is made between “personal” and “social” self.
reasons: review:Quote/back type the marks as double curly quotes; NCERT p26 prints single quotes 'personal' and 'social'. Front is open: 'which other self' also fits the 'biological self' discussed just before in the same section, and 'social' is a near-guess; name the pair or blank 'social' with the sentence shown

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: NCERT: stress is like what? (It gives energy, increases human arousal and affects performance.)
cards.back: Stress is like electricity. It gives energy, increases human arousal and affects performance.
cards.quote: Stress is like electricity. It gives energy, increases human arousal and affects performance.

source.section: Nature, Types and Sources of Stress

reasons: review:Open analogy question: from the front alone fuel, fire, a drug or a double-edged sword also fit 'gives energy, increases arousal, affects performance'; only recall of NCERT's word gives electricity. Blank the word in the sentence or ask 'NCERT compares stress to which thing that can fuse bulbs if to

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: How many life changes make up the Presumptive Stressful Life Events Scale for the Indian population?
cards.back:
Fifty-one
It is a self-rating questionnaire made up of fifty-one life changes, which a person may have experienced.
cards.quote: A measure of stressful life events based on the above scale known as the Presumptive Stressful Life Events Scale has been developed for the Indian population by Singh, Kaur and Kaur. It is a self-rating questionnaire made up of fifty-one life changes, which a person may have experienced.

source.section: A Measure of Stressful Life Events (Box 3.1)

reasons: review:Bare count (fifty-one items) of an Indian scale in a box is trivia; the scale's name/authors or use matter more than the number.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Researchers estimate that stress plays an important role in ____ to ____ per cent of all physical illnesses.
cards.back: Researchers estimate that stress plays an important role in fifty to seventy per cent of all physical illnesses.
cards.quote: Researchers estimate that stress plays an important role in fifty to seventy per cent of all physical illnesses.
reasons: review:bare statistic (50 to 70 per cent), low exam value

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Studies also reveal that ____ per cent of medical visits are primarily for stress-related symptoms.
cards.back: Studies also reveal that sixty per cent of medical visits are primarily for stress-related symptoms.
cards.quote: Studies also reveal that sixty per cent of medical visits are primarily for stress-related symptoms.
reasons: review:bare statistic (60 per cent of medical visits), low exam value

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: What is lifestyle?
cards.back: Lifestyle is the overall pattern of decisions and behaviours that determine a person's health and quality of life.
cards.quote: Lifestyle is the overall pattern of decisions and behaviours that determine a person's health and quality of life.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Avoidance-oriented coping strategy (Endler and Parker).
cards.back: This involves denying or minimising the seriousness of the situation; it also involves conscious suppression of stressful thoughts
cards.quote: Avoidance-oriented Strategy : This involves denying or minimising the seriousness of the situation; it also involves conscious suppression of stressful thoughts
reasons: review:Endler and Parker avoidance-oriented strategy parallels task-oriented (must); should be must; quote and back are cut mid-sentence; NCERT continues "and their replacement by self-protective thoughts"

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Which type of coping is this? “I made a plan of action and followed it”.
cards.back: They can act to reduce the threat value of the event. For example “I made a plan of action and followed it”.
cards.quote: They can act to reduce the threat value of the event. For example “I made a plan of action and followed it”.
reasons: review:back does not state the answer (problem-focused) and opens with dangling "They"; example card must name the concept; "I made a plan of action and followed it" fits both problem-focused and task-oriented coping

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: What is informational social support?
cards.back: Family and friends also provide informational support about stressful events.
cards.quote: Family and friends also provide informational support about stressful events.
reasons: review:circular sentence ("provide informational support"), no real definition or example; better as one list card of tangible/informational/emotional support

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: NCERT gives two basic, conflicting views of abnormal behaviour. How does the first approach view it?
cards.back: The first approach views abnormal behaviour as a deviation from social norms.
cards.quote: The first approach views abnormal behaviour as a deviation from social norms.

source.section: Concepts of Abnormality and Psychological Disorders

reasons: review:Front depends on the ordinal 'first approach'; a student cannot derive first vs second from content, and 'maladaptive' fits the same front. Reword e.g. 'Abnormality as deviation from social norms: which view is this?' or ask for both views.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Example: how may a competitive society and a cooperative society (such as India) differ on aggressive behaviour?
cards.back: Thus, a society whose culture values competition and assertiveness may accept aggressive behaviour, whereas one that emphasises cooperation and family values (such as in India) may consider aggressive behaviour as unacceptable or even abnormal.
cards.quote: Thus, a society whose culture values competition and assertiveness may accept aggressive behaviour, whereas one that emphasises cooperation and family values (such as in India) may consider aggressive behaviour as unacceptable or even abnormal.

source.section: Concepts of Abnormality and Psychological Disorders

reasons: review:Illustrative example (aggression in competitive vs cooperative society), not a testable definition or list; low exam value.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: NCERT gives two basic, conflicting views of abnormal behaviour. How does the second approach view it?
cards.back: The second approach views abnormal behaviour as maladaptive.
cards.quote: The second approach views abnormal behaviour as maladaptive.

source.section: Concepts of Abnormality and Psychological Disorders

reasons: review:Same as first-approach card: ordinal 'second approach' is not derivable; answer is only obtainable by eliminating the other view. Reword to name the view without the ordinal.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Which three psychological disorders does NCERT name as linked to genetic factors?
cards.back: Genetic factors have been linked to bipolar and related disorders, schizophrenia, intellectual disability and other psychological disorders.
cards.quote: Genetic factors have been linked to bipolar and related disorders, schizophrenia, intellectual disability and other psychological disorders.
reasons: review:Next sentence on the same page says genetic/biochemical factors are involved in schizophrenia, depression, anxiety, so a student can validly name different disorders; front must anchor 'Genetic factors have been linked to ...'. Also 'and other disorders' is in the back.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Cognitive model: which two adjectives does NCERT use for the assumptions and attitudes people may hold about themselves?
cards.back: People may hold assumptions and attitudes about themselves that are irrational and inaccurate.
cards.quote: People may hold assumptions and attitudes about themselves that are irrational and inaccurate.
reasons: review:'Two adjectives' (irrational, inaccurate) have obvious synonyms (illogical, unrealistic, incorrect); next sentence uses 'illogical'. Make it a term/key_line with the blanks irrational and inaccurate, or ask what the model says about the assumptions.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: What is dissociative identity disorder, often referred to as multiple personality?
cards.back: Dissociative identity disorder, often referred to as multiple personality, is the most dramatic of the dissociative disorders.
cards.quote: Dissociative identity disorder, often referred to as multiple personality, is the most dramatic of the dissociative disorders.
reasons: review:Back ('the most dramatic of the dissociative disorders') does not define DID; a correct definition would not match it. Use NCERT's 'the person assumes alternate personalities that may or may not be aware of each other'.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Table 4.2: academics of individuals with severe and profound intellectual disability.
cards.back: No academic skills
cards.quote: No academic skills

source.section: Table 4.2 Characteristics of Individuals with Different Levels of Intellectual Disability

reasons: review:'No academic skills' is trivially guessable table filler with no memory value.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: The purpose of the relationship is to help the client to ____ the psychological problems being faced by her or him.
cards.back: The purpose of the relationship is to help the client to solve the psychological problems being faced by her or him.
cards.quote: The purpose of the relationship is to help the client to solve the psychological problems being faced by her or him.
reasons: review:Blank 'solve' is a generic verb (solve/resolve/overcome all fit) and carries no marks; low exam value.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Is it advisable to begin psychotherapy without first making a clinical formulation?
cards.back:
No.
It is not advisable to start psychotherapy without a clinical formulation.
cards.quote: It is not advisable to start psychotherapy without a clinical formulation.

source.section: Steps in the Formulation of a Client's Problem

reasons: review:Yes/no front is guessable (50 percent) and tests nothing a student must recall; the useful content (clinical formulation first) is better as a statement.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: A young person started smoking during exam preparation and felt relief from anxiety. Name the antecedent and maintaining factors.
cards.back:
Antecedent: anxiety-provoking situation. Maintaining: relief from anxiety.
Thus, anxiety-provoking situation becomes the causative or antecedent factor. The feeling of relief becomes the maintaining factor for him to continue smoking.
cards.quote: Thus, anxiety-provoking situation becomes the causative or antecedent factor. The feeling of relief becomes the maintaining factor for him to continue smoking.
reasons: review:Case-story filler: the exam-smoking case is an illustration; the testable point is the definitions of antecedent and maintaining factors. Front already gives away the maintaining factor (relief from anxiety) and "exam preparation" is an equally valid antecedent answer to NCERT's "anxiety-provoking s

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: The aim of the treatment is to extinguish or eliminate the faulty behaviours and ____ them with adaptive behaviour patterns.
cards.back: The aim of the treatment is to extinguish or eliminate the faulty behaviours and substitute them with adaptive behaviour patterns.
cards.quote: The aim of the treatment is to extinguish or eliminate the faulty behaviours and substitute them with adaptive behaviour patterns.
reasons: review:Blank 'substitute' has synonym 'replace'; generic verb, not mark-bearing.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: A child gives trouble in eating dinner. Which is the antecedent operation and which the consequent operation?
cards.back:
Antecedent: less food at tea time. Consequent: praise for eating dinner.
The antecedent operation is the reduction of food at tea time and the consequent operation is praising the child for eating dinner.
cards.quote: The antecedent operation is the reduction of food at tea time and the consequent operation is praising the child for eating dinner.
reasons: review:Case-story filler (child, dinner, tea time); not a point worth a CUET student's memory by itself. Front does not determine the answer: "less food at tea time" and "praise" cannot be derived from the question, a student could give other operations.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: In client-centred therapy, what does the therapist show (empathy and unconditional positive regard)?
cards.back: The therapist shows empathy, i.e. understanding the client's experience as if it were her/his own, is warm and has unconditional positive regard, i.e. total acceptance of the client as s/he is.
cards.quote: The therapist shows empathy, i.e. understanding the client's experience as if it were her/his own, is warm and has unconditional positive regard, i.e. total acceptance of the client as s/he is.
reasons: review:Front gives away the answer in brackets (empathy and unconditional positive regard) and duplicates the separate empathy and UPR cards.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: SKY has been used as a public health intervention technique to alleviate PTSD in survivors of ____.
cards.back: SKY has been used as a public health intervention technique to alleviate PTSD in survivors of mass disasters.
cards.quote: SKY has been used as a public health intervention technique to alleviate PTSD in survivors of mass disasters.
reasons: review:Trivia (survivors of 'mass disasters'); low CUET value.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Attitudes cannot be observed from outside. Of what are they a part, along with an emotional component?
cards.back:
Cognition.
They are part of cognition, along with an emotional component, and cannot be observed from outside.
cards.quote: They are part of cognition, along with an emotional component, and cannot be observed from outside.
reasons: review:Odd, low-value NCERT sentence; the A-B-C components are already covered, and "part of cognition" is trivia. "Of what are they a part?" has other defensible answers (attitude system, personality, social cognition); the answer "cognition" cannot be reached from the front.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: On the nuclear research scale, how does a rating of 1 compare with a rating of 5 on extremeness?
cards.back: Taking the nuclear research example given above, a rating of 1 is as extreme as a rating of 5 : they are only in the opposite directions (valence).
cards.quote: Taking the nuclear research example given above, a rating of 1 is as extreme as a rating of 5 : they are only in the opposite directions (valence).
reasons: review:Illustration only: the 1-5 nuclear-research scale is not shown on the card and the back says 'given above'; the concept is already carried by the extremeness definition.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: An army driver, sole survivor of a mission, becomes a community leader. Which factor in attitude formation?
cards.back:
Personal experiences
Through a purely personal experience this individual evolved a strong positive attitude towards community upliftment.
cards.quote: Through a purely personal experience this individual evolved a strong positive attitude towards community upliftment.
reasons: review:Case-story filler (army driver anecdote); the factor 'Personal experiences' is already covered by the list card.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: What valence would a neutral attitude have?
cards.back: A neutral attitude would have neither positive nor negative valence.
cards.quote: A neutral attitude would have neither positive nor negative valence.
reasons: review:Circular trivia: a neutral attitude has neither positive nor negative valence follows from the word neutral; not a mark-carrying fact.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Festinger and Carlsmith's $ 1 group: what did the students conclude about the experiment, and on what basis?
cards.back: on the basis of their behaviour (telling others that the experiment was interesting, for only a small amount of money), they concluded that their attitude towards the experiment was positive (‘I would not have told a lie for this small amount of money, which means that the experiment was actually interesting’).
cards.quote: on the basis of their behaviour (telling others that the experiment was interesting, for only a small amount of money), they concluded that their attitude towards the experiment was positive (‘I would not have told a lie for this small amount of money, which means that the experiment was actually interesting’).
reasons: review:Front says 'the experiment' but never states what it was (students told others a boring experiment was interesting for $ 1), so a student without the box cannot answer; two-part question (conclusion and basis); back opens with a lowercase fragment.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Behaviour of people in crowds is ____ and there is no interdependence among members.
cards.back: Behaviour of people in crowds is irrational and there is no interdependence among members.
cards.quote: Behaviour of people in crowds is irrational and there is no interdependence among members.
reasons: review:Ambiguous: 'irrational' has plausible alternatives (impulsive, unpredictable); not a forced fill.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: When people have common ____ or goals, they get together and form a group which may facilitate their goal attainment.
cards.back: When people have common motives or goals, they get together and form a group which may facilitate their goal attainment.
cards.quote: When people have common motives or goals, they get together and form a group which may facilitate their goal attainment.
reasons: review:Ambiguous: 'motives' has equal fits (aims, interests, objectives) before 'or goals'.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Cohesiveness refers to the ____ or ‘we feeling’ or a sense of belongingness to the group.
cards.back: Cohesiveness refers to the team spirit or ‘we feeling’ or a sense of belongingness to the group.
cards.quote: Cohesiveness refers to the team spirit or ‘we feeling’ or a sense of belongingness to the group.
reasons: review:Ambiguous: 'team spirit' competes with 'togetherness' (given in the definition sentence); two-word blank.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Formal vs informal groups: the difference in how the functions of the group are stated.
cards.back: These groups differ in the degree to which the functions of the group are stated explicitly and formally. The functions of a formal group are explicitly stated as in the case of an office organisation.
cards.quote: These groups differ in the degree to which the functions of the group are stated explicitly and formally. The functions of a formal group are explicitly stated as in the case of an office organisation.
reasons: review:Difference card gives only the formal side; back opens 'These groups differ...' with no antecedent and never states the informal side, so the contrast cannot be recalled or marked. Formal vs informal is a headed contrast (Review Question 1) and should be must; better built on the structure sentence

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: For ingroup members, we use the word ‘we’ while for outgroup members, the word ‘____’ is used.
cards.back: For ingroup members, we use the word ‘we’ while for outgroup members, the word ‘they’ is used.
cards.quote: For ingroup members, we use the word ‘we’ while for outgroup members, the word ‘they’ is used.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: In Tajfel's experiment, preference for paintings by which two artists formed the groups?
cards.back: British schoolboys expressed their preference for paintings by two artists — Vassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee.
cards.quote: British schoolboys expressed their preference for paintings by two artists — Vassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee.
reasons: review:Not important: Names of the two painters (Kandinsky, Klee) are experimental trivia, not exam-tested content.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Latane's experiment: what group sizes were used?
cards.back: individuals were either alone, or in groups of two, four and six.
cards.quote: They varied the group size; individuals were either alone, or in groups of two, four and six.
reasons: review:Not important: Group sizes (alone, two, four, six) are experimental trivia, not exam-tested content.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: Whatever the initial position in the group, this position becomes much ____ as a result of discussions in the group.
cards.back: Whatever the initial position in the group, this position becomes much stronger as a result of discussions in the group.
cards.quote: Whatever the initial position in the group, this position becomes much stronger as a result of discussions in the group.

cards.subject: psychology
cards.front: What kind of repercussions may group polarisation sometimes have?
cards.back:
Dangerous repercussions
This may sometimes have dangerous repercussions as groups may take extreme positions, i.e. from very weak to very strong decisions.
cards.quote: This strengthening of the group's initial position as a result of group interaction and discussion is referred to as group polarisation. This may sometimes have dangerous repercussions as groups may take extreme positions, i.e. from very weak to very strong decisions.
reasons: review:Blank is an adjective with obvious synonyms (harmful, serious, bad); 'dangerous repercussions' is a hedged ('may sometimes') consequence phrase, not a mark-carrying fact. Drop or turn into the definition of group polarisation.
